title: Whom he sees not (1 John 4:20)
hookLine: how can you love God whom you don't see if you don't love your brother
tomorrow: keep yourselves in the love of God

cards: In Dostoevsky's novel The Brothers Karamazov, the old monk Zosima tells about a doctor who once admitted something embarrassing. The more he loved humanity in general, the less he loved actual people in particular.
In his dreams he'd gladly die for the human race. But put him in a room with one real person for a day, and he couldn't stand the way they blew their nose or how slowly they ate.
Some mornings that doctor is in the mirror. John, near the end of his first letter, catches the same trick and turns it toward God.

teach.h: IF ANY MAN SAY, I LOVE GOD...
teach.b: John has just said that God is love and that love casts out fear. Then he brings it down to earth with a thud.

The Douay-Rheims: "If any man say, I love God, and hateth his brother; he is a liar. For he that loveth not his brother, whom he seeth, how can he love God, whom he seeth not?" Liar is a strong word, and John means it.
Not mistaken, not still growing: lying. Love for God can stay very safe. God doesn't interrupt you, borrow your car, or chew loudly.

teach.h: NO ONE HAS EVER SEEN GOD.
teach.b: Earlier in this chapter John says no one has ever seen God. So where does love for the unseen God get tested? On the seen.
The coworker. The brother-in-law. The roommate.
If you can't manage the one in front of you, whose face you know, what makes you think you're managing the one you've never seen?
And right after, he spells out the commandment: whoever loves God must love his brother also. The two loves aren't rivals.
They're one love, facing two directions. Catholics act this out at Mass.

teach.h: THE SIGN OF PEACE BEFORE COMMUNION.
teach.b: Just before Communion, before receiving the Lord they cannot see, people may turn to whoever is next to them and offer a sign of peace: a handshake, a nod, sometimes to a stranger, sometimes to the family member they were arguing with in the car.

teach.h: WHOM HE SEETH, AND WHOM HE SEETH NOT.
teach.b: Jesus said something like it: if you remember at the altar that your brother has something against you, go first and be reconciled, then come back and offer your gift.

how: At Mass, after the Lord's Prayer and before Communion, Catholics may exchange a sign of peace with the people around them, and the Church teaches that love of God and love of neighbor are inseparable.

games.q: what does “whom he sees not” mean?
o: God, loved by loving the people you can see
a stranger you've never met in person
the dead, who can no longer be seen

games.q: whom he sees not — tap the pairs.
p: says he loves God, hates his brother

s: John says hating your brother while loving God is a small inconsistency
he calls it a lie: love for the unseen God is tested on the brother you can see.
the same chapter says no one has ever seen God
1 John 4:12. so love for God shows up in love for the people we do see.
at Mass the sign of peace comes just before Communion
people turn to whoever is near them before receiving the Lord.

games.q: you're on your way to Mass, and you just argued with your brother in the car. now he's in the pew beside you, and the sign of peace is coming. what does the reading point you toward?
o: skip it and focus on God.
offer him peace, because love for God shows up in love for him.
wait for him to apologize first.
games.why: John asks how you can love God whom you don't see if you don't love the brother you do. Jesus says it too: be reconciled first, then bring your gift.

practice: Think of the person nearest your life right now, the one you'll see today: not the easiest, just the nearest.
Picture their face, the things that wear on you too, and find one small way to love them: a kind word, patience with a habit, listening to the end of a story.
If you pray, hold them before God by name; if not, look at them kindly in your mind.

wordCard.voice: Whom he sees not. First John four: love for the God no one has seen is tested on the brother and sister we can see. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: brother (1 John 4:20). in the letter it means fellow believers, men and women alike.

carryVoice: Your line: love the one you see. One love, facing two directions. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: If any man say, I love God, and hateth his brother; he is a liar. For he that loveth not his brother, whom he seeth, how can he love God, whom he seeth not?

sources.ref: Fyodor Dostoevsky, The Brothers Karamazov, Book 2, chapter 4
